release: 1.99.1
LLVM version: 23.1.1
report.scope: Five implementations of the same Rosenbrock descent and complete final vector. fwp-ad records and reverses derivatives; the other four use the explicit derivative. Comparing fwp-ad to a peer includes general AD work and representation costs, not pure compiler overhead. fwp-explicit uses immutable lists and intermediate pairs/lists; fwp-packed generates a packed array per update, reading the previous array at checked indices. C/Rust reuse two contiguous buffers. Explicit formulas preserve their multiplication order, but reverse AD may round differently. All outputs are checked against an independent Python derivative with absolute/relative tolerance 1e-10. Per-implementation timed outputs must repeat exactly. Inputs and update counts are compile-time constants. C/Rust/fwp formatting and allocation strategies differ. Timings include fresh-process startup, initialization, descent, complete output and teardown; compilation and instrumentation are excluded. The zero-update case includes initialization and formatting, so it is not pure startup time. Raw derivative buffers and managed charge are observed separately for fwp only. Separate uninstrumented process RSS includes all process storage; do not add it to allocation peaks. The original two fwp forms must reproduce the recorded managed/raw profiles exactly; timing peers are recompiled and remeasured together. All samples and compile commands are retained. For at least 199 updates, packed fwp must make fewer managed allocation requests with no higher managed peak than explicit-list fwp. Retains and timings are reported without a speed threshold; this is a program-representation experiment, not a compiler change.
